main_text.l: Alokaisar, eidem Idoli nomen quod في مشارق
الشام i.e. in arientali Syria Damascena plaga positum à tribus
non una cultum refert Safioddinus. بغ Bag, a quo
(ut quibusdam, teste Abul Feda videtur) urbs Bagdad
nomen cepit, ut Persicè Bag dedit, seu Bagi donum so-
net, Persarum seu Indorum, à quibus oriundus Eunu-
chus iste qui hoc nomen imposuit, potiùs quam Ara-
bum Idolum fuisse puto: يعبدونه في الشرق [?] inquit, i.
in Oriente illud colebant. Idoli à Bani Salim culti, ac
à Gamio Ebn AbdolVazza ipsius æditiuo pro merito suo
tractati, nomen licèt non expresserit AlEirauzabadius,
non indigna tamen sunt memoratu quæ narrat.
Spectante sc. æditiuo, sed officii sui (ut videtur) neg-
ligentiore, accurrentes vulpeculæ duæ Idoli con-
fcensi caput urinâ cansurcârunt: ille indignum cul-
tu suo Dominum ratus, qui hæc inultus pateretur, in
hæc verba prorupit,
أرب يبول التعلبان براهمة لقد ذلت من بالت علمة تعالب
i. e. Num ille Dominus est, super cujus caput mingunt

l.i: Certè vilè est super quem minxerint vulpes.

main_text.l: O Solaimenses, certè nec obest hic nec prodest, nec largitur,
nec impedit, correptumque Idolum confregit. Contigit
hoc post Mahammedem natum, qui in boni facti me-
moriam nomen ejus غاوي بن
عبد العزى Gavi Ebn Abdiluzza, i. e. "Errans filius cultoris Vzza,
magis fausto, sc. راشد بن عبد ربه Rashed Ebn Abd
Rabbebi, i e. Orthodoxus filius cultoris Dominisui, com-
mutavit. Nec magis injurii erga Deum suum Ban-
i Hanifa, seu Hanifida, quos Idolum è massâ quâdam

page.notes: Arabic passages are transcribed from the scan and may contain small errors; doubtful letters are not individually marked. The Arabic on the first line of the verse and in the "Bag" entry was read with uncertainty and should be checked against the original. The first paragraph begins mid-entry, so it is marked as a continuation from the previous page. The catchword "confectum" is set alone at the right below the last full line.
